subject: Cloud Computing
title: Data Versioning and Lineage
description: A micro-lesson that makes Data Versioning and Lineage usable.

hook.text: Your ML model's accuracy dropped overnight. Something changed in the training data. But what? And when?

buildup.text: Data versioning tracks changes to datasets over time, like Git tracks code changes.

discovery.text: Data lineage maps the entire journey: where data came from, how it was transformed, and where it ended up.

twist.text: Without lineage, debugging data issues is like detective work without clues. You're guessing in the dark.

climax.text: Tools like dbt, Apache Atlas, and cloud-native catalogs now make data lineage trackable and searchable.

punchline.text: Version your data like you version your code. Track every change.

quiz.question: What does data lineage track?
options: Where data came from, how it was transformed, and where it ended up
How many users accessed the data in the last month
The cost of storing data across different cloud regions

details.summary: Data versioning tracks changes to datasets over time, enabling rollback and reproducibility. Data lineage traces how data flows through pipelines from source to destination. Together they provide the audit trail needed for debugging, compliance, and trust in data.
details.whyItMatters: Without versioning and lineage, diagnosing bad data is nearly impossible. Knowing what changed, when, and how it propagated is essential for regulated industries and machine learning reproducibility.
takeaways: Versioning enables rollback to any previous dataset state
Lineage tracks data from source through every transformation
Essential for compliance, debugging, and ML reproducibility

faq.question: What tools provide data lineage?
faq.answer: Apache Atlas, DataHub, and OpenLineage capture lineage from data pipelines. Cloud providers offer lineage in Azure Purview and Google Dataplex. dbt tracks lineage for SQL transformations. Modern data catalogs integrate lineage visualization.

faq.question: How does data versioning work in practice?
faq.answer: Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg version datasets using transaction logs that record every change. You can query any historical version using time travel. For ML datasets, tools like DVC version data files alongside code in Git repositories.
